title: Ackee and Saltfish with Fried Dumplings and Plantain
summary: Flaked saltfish folded gently with ackee, peppers and aromatics, served alongside crisp fried dumplings and caramelised plantain.
equipment: large frying pan or sauté pan

ingredients.item: spring onions, cut into 5 cm lengths
Scotch bonnet chilli, seeded and finely chopped (optional)
fine sea salt or table salt
ripe plantains (yellow with black spots), sliced on the diagonal

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Soak 225 g salt cod in cold water in the fridge overnight, changing the water 2-3 times, then drain.

steps.title: Poach
steps.text: Simmer the cod in fresh water for 10 min, drain, cool and flake, removing any skin or bones.

steps.title: Dough
steps.text: Mix 250 g flour, 1 tsp baking powder and ½ tsp salt, stir in 150 ml cold water to a firm dough, knead for 2 min, rest for 10 min, then divide into 8 balls and flatten.

steps.title: Fry dumplings
steps.text: Heat 1 cm of oil in a pan and fry the dumplings, turning, until golden and cooked through, 10-12 min, then drain.

steps.title: Fry plantain
steps.text: In the same oil, fry the sliced plantains until caramelised, 2-3 min per side, then drain.

steps.title: Soften
steps.text: Heat 3 tbsp coconut oil and cook the onion, red pepper, garlic, spring onion, thyme and chilli until soft, 5 min.

steps.title: Addfish
steps.text: Stir in the flaked saltfish and tomato wedges and cook for 3-4 min.

steps.title: Ackee
steps.text: Fold in the drained ackee very gently so it stays in pieces, warm through for 3-4 min, then season with ½ tsp pepper.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Remove the thyme stems and serve with the dumplings and plantain.

tips: Start soaking the salt cod the night before, changing the water a few times to draw out excess salt.
Fold the ackee in gently at the end so the delicate pieces don't break apart.
Fry the plantain in the same oil once the dumplings are done for an extra layer of flavour.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Best eaten freshly cooked; any leftovers can be kept covered in the fridge for up to 2 days and reheated until hot throughout before serving. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
